name: Oberheim Matrix-1000
source: Oberheim Matrix-1000 Owner's Manual (1988; archive.org synthmanual-oberheim-matrix-1000-owners-manual, read from the page images): quick start + Bank Lock pp.8-9, selecting patches from MIDI pp.18-19, Channel p.20-21, Extended Functions pp.23-26 and 36-39 (Memory Protect = Ext Funct 6), Data Dump pp.33-35, MIDI summary + SysEx data format pp.41-45 (opcodes 01/03/04/06/07/0A/0B/0C/0D/0E), Single Patch Data Format pp.46-51, Tables 1-3 pp.52-53, Global Parameters format + Device Inquiry/ID + universal Bank Select p.54-55, active controllers/NRPN p.56. Cross-checked against: Edisyn edisyn/synth/oberheimmatrix1000/OberheimMatrix1000.java (github.com/eclab/edisyn; param-number <-> dump-offset tables match the manual for all 96 params; 0A+PC+0C program change; 0A+01 store; 04 04 edit-buffer request; sign-extension notes) and its git history (Jan 2018 'Send/Write Bugfix'); KnobKraft-orm synths/oberheim-matrix1000/Matrix1000.cpp + adaptations/Matrix1000.py (0E store, 0A+0C+04-01 read, device inquiry, 80 dummy splits in a bank dump, a real device-captured dump of patch 216); Matrix-6R SysEx spec (youngmonkey.ca, opcode 05 'quick patch edit'); Opcode Galaxy 'Matrix-6/6R/1000 Editor' tech pub (parameter meanings/ranges); wolzow.mindworks.ee m1k-midi-spec + m1k-firmware (archived 2019: param 53/29 firmware bugs, undocumented 08/09, NRPN state); Tauntek Matrix1000Firmware.htm + mtrx1kv120 ReadmeM1K.txt (v1.20); untergeek.de firmware V1.21 page + M1000-Parameters-V1.2.pdf; GliGli v1.16 blog post. Byte layout validated by decoding the 200 factory RAM patches (Edisyn resources/Matrix1000Banks.zip, BNK000/BNK100.syx: 200/200 checksums OK, every signed byte correctly sign-extended) and KnobKraft's hardware capture of patch 216.

oberheim.deviceByte: None. Oberheim Matrix messages carry no channel or unit number (only 0E has a group-mode unit ID). Every Matrix-1000 on the cable acts on them; the MIDI channel only matters for Program Change / notes / CCs.

formats.singlePatchData: F0 10 06 01 <num 0-99> <268 nybbles> <checksum> F7 = 275 bytes. Received: stored into slot <num> of the CURRENT bank (set it first with 0A); if that slot is the one playing, it is reloaded into the edit buffer. Ignored when Memory Protect is on. Transmitted: reply to 04-1 (and to 04-0 x100) and, per KnobKraft, to 04-4.
formats.patchToEditBuffer: F0 10 06 0D 00 <268 nybbles> <checksum> F7 = 275 bytes. Received into the edit buffer only (sounds immediately, nothing stored). Manual: wait >= 10 ms after it.
formats.request: F0 10 06 04 <type> <num> F7. type 0 = 100 patches of the current bank + dummies + master; 1 = patch <num> of the current bank; 3 = master parameters; 4 = edit buffer (<num> = 0).
formats.remoteParam: F0 10 06 06 <param 0-98> <value> F7. Edits one parameter of the edit buffer. Value: unsigned params raw; signed params masked to 7 bits (two's complement, the unit sign-extends bit 6 into bit 7). VCF frequency (param 21) is the one 7-bit unsigned value (the manual's 'parameter 121' is a typo). Range-check before sending. Bit-packed params (07, 06, 08, 16, 17, 18, 25, 26, 57, 58, 59, ...) take the whole field value.
formats.remoteMatrix: F0 10 06 0B <slot 0-9> <source 0-20> <amount & 7F> <dest 0-32> F7. Source 0 or dest 0 deletes the slot (send 00 00 00).
formats.setBank: F0 10 06 0A <bank 0-9> F7. Sets the current bank for later Program Change / 01 / 04-1 / 04-0 AND turns Bank Lock on (decimal point lit).
formats.unlockBank: F0 10 06 0C F7. Turns Bank Lock off (the bank number stays).
formats.storeEditBuffer: F0 10 06 0E <num 0-99> <bank 0-9> <id> F7; id = 0 when group mode is off (7F = any unit in group mode). Stores the edit buffer into bank/num.
formats.masterData: F0 10 06 03 03 <344 nybbles> <checksum> F7 = 351 bytes (byte 4 = 03 = Matrix-1000 version code). 172 unpacked bytes: 1-7 vibrato, 8 master tune (signed), 11 basic channel 0-15, 12 omni, 13 controllers enable, 14 patch-change enable, 17-20 pedal 1/pedal 2/lever 2/lever 3 CC numbers, 32 MIDI echo, 34 transpose (signed), 35 mono mode, 36-161 group-enable bits (one per patch, LS bit first), 164 bend range, 165 bank lock (MSB/high nybble only, 80h), 166 units, 167 unit number, 168 group mode (MSB), 169 unison, 170 volume invert, 171 memory protect.
formats.splitPatchData: F0 10 06 02 <num> <dummy data> <checksum> F7, transmit-only filler after a 04-0 bank request (Matrix-6 compatibility). Ignore.
formats.deviceInquiry: F0 7E <ch|7F> 06 01 F7 -> F0 7E <basic ch 0-15> 06 02 10 06 00 02 00 <r0> <r1> <r2> <r3> F7 (15 bytes): 10 = Oberheim, 06 00 = Matrix-6/6R/1000 family, 02 00 = Matrix-1000, r0-r3 = 4 ASCII chars of the firmware version, right justified (v1.10 = 20 31 31 30 = ' 110').
formats.universalBankSelect: F0 7F <id 7F> 02 01 <chan> <x> <x> <x> <x> <bank 0-9> 00 F7 (manual p.55; not needed -- use 0A).

oberheim.nybbles: Each unpacked byte b is sent as two bytes, LOW nybble first: [b & 0F, b >> 4]. Decode b = d[i] | (d[i+1] << 4).
oberheim.checksum: (sum of the 134 UNPACKED bytes) & 7F, sent once after the nybbles (master data: sum of the 172 unpacked bytes & 7F).
oberheim.valueEncoding: Unsigned params: the byte is the value. Signed params ('7 (signed)', '6 (signed)' in the manual) are stored as full 8-bit two's complement, i.e. sign-extended through bit 7: -14 -> F2h (nybbles 02 0F), +45 -> 2Dh. Writing a 7-bit two's complement with bit 7 clear (-14 as 72h) makes the patch sound wrong -- this is what Edisyn originally hit and misdiagnosed as a 0D 'corrupts patches' firmware bug; fixed by sign-extending (Edisyn commits b5cdc52 + df837e8, 13 Jan 2018, which also removed its slot-199 scratch workaround). Remote edit (06/0B) instead takes value & 7F.

examples.decodedFactory000: BNK000.syx message 0 (TOTOHORN): F0 10 06 01 00 | 02 04 0E 04 0B 04 ... -> name 'BNK0: 00'; byte 8 = 01 00 -> keyboard mode 1 (rotate); byte 9 = 04 02 -> DCO1 freq 36; byte 13 = 03 00 -> pulse+wave; byte 19 = 02 0F -> F2h -> detune -14; byte 26 = 09 01 -> VCF 25; byte 87 = 0D 02 -> +45; byte 89 = 08 0D -> D8h -> -40; slot 0 = 01 00 / 0F 03 / 0B 00 -> Env1 -> VCA1 level, +63; checksum 15h (sum 2837 & 7F) then F7.

firmware.check: The 3-digit version flashes on the display at power-on (e.g. 111, 116, 120) and comes back in the device-ID reply.

versions.note: Early units. Needs Oberheim ECO 1207 (comparator PULSE -> 68B50 CTS) before ANY later EPROM will run (Tauntek).

Factory (1.11 = last Oberheim release). Remote edit of param 53 (Env 1 sustain) writes Env 2 amplitude; param 29 (VCA 2 by Env 2) has no effect except in a whole patch; NRPN not working; every edit that changes a voice's update stack rebuilds it for all six voices (60-90 ms, CV refresh stops meanwhile), so fast sweeps choke. Opcode's editor requires >= 1.10.
GliGli: Nordcore fixes + NRPN fix + faster matrix rebuild by dropping stale queued edits (values may jump) + unison detune on CC94 (0-127, always active). SysEx unchanged.

Tauntek (Bob Grieb; Europe via untergeek): Nordcore fixes, GliGli detune (CC94), NRPN incl. inc/dec fixed, 20 params updated in real time (1,3,4,7,9,11,13,14,17,19,21,22,23,24,25,27,28,30,31,32), value shown on the LEDs while edited over MIDI. 1.21 also fixes Reassign w/ Rob. SysEx unchanged. RECOMMENDED.

firmware.recommendation: 1.20/1.21 for live editing; 1.16 acceptable; 1.11 works for dumps/stores but keep live edits slow and route params 29/53 through 0D.

banks.note: RAM (battery-backed): writable unless Memory Protect is on
RAM (battery-backed): writable unless Memory Protect is on

programs.note: Patches 000-999 = 10 banks x 100. Select: 0A <bank> (bank lock on) -> Program Change 0-99 -> 0C (unlock). Without bank lock, Program Change 0-127 selects 000-127 regardless of bank. Every bank is readable (0A bank, 0C, 04 01 n); only 000-199 are writable. No names are stored -- classicNames[bank*100 + n] are the factory names from the Matrix-1000 Patchbook (via Edisyn): exact for ROM 200-999, factory-only for RAM 000-199.

areas.request: F0 10 06 0A 00 F7, F0 10 06 0C F7, then 100 x F0 10 06 04 01 <n> F7 (one at a time) -- or F0 10 06 04 00 00 F7 once (100 x 01 + 80 dummy 02 + 1 x 03, ~12 s, cannot be stopped)

backup.restore: Memory Protect off. F0 10 06 0A <bank> F7, then the saved 01 messages unchanged (each carries its slot number) >= 10 ms apart (manual; use ~100 ms), then F0 10 06 0C F7. Factory 000-199 restore: Edisyn resources/Matrix1000Banks.zip.
backup.notInSysex: Nothing else is lost by a battery failure that SysEx can't restore except the master block (restorable via a received 03 message -- not implemented; writing it also rewrites all 1000 group-enable bits).

setup: Firmware: watch the number at power-on (or the device-ID reply). 1.20/1.21 (Tauntek) recommended; 1.16 OK; 1.10/1.11 work but live edits are slow and Env 1 sustain / VCA 2-by-Env 2 only change via whole-patch sends. A 1.03 unit needs ECO 1207 before any upgrade.
Channel mode (press Select until Channel lights): + / - to the editor's channel 1-16. Avoid 'on' (OMNI; transmits on ch 1) and G1-G9 (mono/guitar mode).
Ext Funct 6 = Pof (Memory Protect OFF): with it on, stores, 01 dumps and panel copies are ignored silently.
Ext Funct 2 = Eot (MIDI Echo OFF): with it on, everything the editor sends (SysEx too) comes straight back.
Units mode = off (no group mode) so stores use unit ID 0.
Leave Bank Lock off (no decimal point after the first digit); the editor turns it on/off around each bank change.

MIDI patch changes must be enabled (master byte 14; on after a reset -- there is no front-panel switch for it). If program changes do nothing, re-initialise (power on holding Enter -- resets globals, keeps patches 000-199) or fix it with a master-data editor.
Back up banks 0 and 1 (patches 000-199) before storing anything; old units often have a weak RAM battery.
Cable both ways: interface out -> Matrix MIDI IN, Matrix MIDI OUT (not THRU) -> interface in (every read needs the return path).
driverNotes:
New transport 'oberheim' (Matrix-6/6R/1000 SysEx: F0 10 06 ... F7). No existing transport fits: ensoniq shares the low-nybble-first packing but has a channel byte, no checksum and a keypad protocol; nrpn/roland/yamaha differ entirely. (1) FRAMING: out = [F0,10,06,op,...,F7]; no channel/device byte (programChange and notes use channel()). Match incoming on d[1]==10 && d[2]==06 && d[3]==op. Ignore op 02 (dummy splits) and, unless waiting for it, 03. (2) IMAGE: keep a 134-byte mirror (last read or the init image). pack(img) = img.flatMap(b => [b & 0x0F, (b >> 4) & 0x0F]); cks = img.reduce((s,b) => s + b, 0) & 0x7F. unpack(d) = for i in 0..133: d[5+2i] | (d[6+2i] << 4); then if d.length >= 275 check d[273] == cks -- on mismatch reject and report (all 200 factory dumps and a hardware capture carry a valid checksum; Edisyn's recognizer also accepts a 274-byte message without one -- accept that silently). (3) VALUES: param.offset = byte in the 134. Plain: value = byte. bits {shift,width}: value = (byte >> shift) & mask; write keeps the other bits (shared bytes 12, 17, 21, 23, 28, 29; byte 21 bit 1 and byte 18 values 5-7 occur and must survive). encoding 'signed': value = byte >= 128 ? byte - 256 : byte; write byte = value & 0xFF (sign-extended through bit 7 -- REQUIRED, see oberheim.valueEncoding). encoding 'trackSrc': plain 1-20, but a 0 read means 1. encoding 'name6': read c = b < 0x20 ? b + 0x40 : b; write b = c >= 0x40 ? c - 0x40 : c (upper-case 20h-5Fh only); a read of 'BNKb: nn' (plain ASCII, /^BNK\d: \d\d$/) is the 1000's placeholder -- show the classic or stored name instead. Matrix slots (p.slot 0-9, p.field src/amt/dst at 104+3*slot +0/+1/+2): if src or dst becomes 0 write src = dst = 0 (manual: unused slots must be 0/0). (4) READ: requestPatch(): send F0 10 06 04 04 00 F7, wait <= 700 ms for an opcode 01 OR 0D message (KnobKraft's C++ says the 1000 answers with 01; its Python adaptation and Edisyn also accept 0D); unpack -> mirror; return {values, syx}. requestProgram(bi, p): send F0 10 06 0A F7, F0 10 06 0C F7, F0 10 06 04 01

F7 (gap ~20 ms between them) and wait <= 700 ms for 01 with d[4] == p (275 bytes = ~90 ms on the wire); return {values, data: the 134 bytes, syx, name: programs.classicNames[bank*100+p] for banks 2-9}. This does not change the sound or edit buffer. requestBank(bi) (optional, backups): 0A bank, 0C, F0 10 06 04 00 00 F7, collect 100 x 01 by d[4], then wait for the 03 master block (80 x 02 come first) or 15 s; cannot be cancelled. requestSlotName(bi, p): no MIDI needed -- banks 2-9: classicNames[bi*100+p]; banks 0-1: the name this editor stored for that slot (keep a prefs map at writeProgram time) else classicNames (factory content, may be stale). (5) SEND EDIT BUFFER: sendPatch(values) = F0 10 06 0D 00 pack(mirror+values) cks F7; then hold the queue >= 100 ms (manual minimum 10 ms; Edisyn pauses 200 ms after a whole-patch send). Trailing-edge throttle repeated whole sends to one per ~250 ms. Do NOT send opcode 05 (Matrix-6 'quick patch edit' prefix) -- the 1000 doesn't need it (harmless if it does). (6) LIVE EDIT: sendParam(p, v): liveEdit 'sysex': write v into the mirror, then F0 10 06 06 F7 where data = p.encoding == 'signed' ? v & 0x7F : (p.bits ? mirror[p.offset] : v) -- bit params send the whole byte (e.g. dco1Bend + dco1Vibrato on -> 06 07 03). liveEdit 'matrix': write the mirror, then F0 10 06 0B F7 from the slot's three mirror bytes (00 00 00 if src or dst is 0). liveEdit 'none' (name chars): mirror only. Params with a 'bug' field (vca2Env2 = 29, env1Sustain = 53): if the firmware read at probe is < 1.13 (or unknown), send the whole patch (5) instead of 06. Clamp to p.min..p.max before sending (the unit doesn't range-check 06). (7) PACING: coalesce per param/slot (keep only the newest pending value). Default one 06/0B per gapMs = 75 ms (Edisyn's per-parameter pause; on 1.10-1.13 a stack-rebuilding edit takes 60-90 ms and freezes the voices meanwhile). If the probed firmware is >= 1.20, params with fast120: true may go every ~25 ms (Tauntek updates them per 20 ms CV refresh); everything else and every 0B stay at 75 ms (matrix edits always rebuild). On 1.16, stale edits are dropped by the firmware, so faster sends just skip values. After 01/0D/0E: 300 ms before the next Program Change or read (Edisyn: < 200 ms gave failed PCs/writes). (8) PROGRAM CHANGE: programChange(bi, p): F0 10 06 0A F7, [Cn p], F0 10 06 0C F7 (Edisyn's tested order: the PC must arrive while Bank Lock is on, else PC n selects 000-127). Afterwards (~150 ms) requestPatch() to adopt the new edit buffer. Needs patch-change enable (master byte 14). Alternative without SysEx: CC31 127, PC , CC31 0, PC p (leaves Bank Lock on). (9) WRITE: writeProgram(bi in {0,1}, p, values): img = mirror + values; send F0 10 06 0A F7, (20 ms), F0 10 06 01

pack(img) cks F7, (300 ms), F0 10 06 0C F7, (100 ms); return img (134 bytes) for the editor's read-back + sameProgram. If bi/p is the playing patch the 1000 reloads it into the edit buffer. Fallback (manual + KnobKraft C++): 0D image, then F0 10 06 0E

00 F7 (number BEFORE bank; KnobKraft's Python adaptation sends bank first -- wrong per the manual). Memory Protect on = silently ignored -> read-back mismatch -> tell the user 'Ext Funct 6 -> Pof'. Never write banks 2-9. (10) PROBE: send F0 7E 7F 06 01 F7, wait 800 ms for F0 7E 06 02 10 06 00 02 00 r0 r1 r2 r3 F7 (KnobKraft waits >= 200 ms; the 1000 is slow to answer). Save fw = parseInt(ascii r0..r3) / 100 (' 111' -> 1.11; Tauntek's chips should read ' 120'/' 121' -- unverified) and the reported basic channel (offer it if it differs from channel()). No reply -> fall back to requestPatch() (ROMs before 1.10 may lack the inquiry); fw unknown -> treat as 1.11 for (6)/(7). Optional after connect: F0 10 06 04 03 00 F7 -> 03 block; warn if byte 171 (memory protect) != 0, byte 32 (echo) != 0 or byte 14 (patch changes) == 0. Never write the master block. (11) decode(ev): the 1000 has no panel editing, so it never sends parameter changes. Inputs: a Program Change on its basic channel (manual: patch changes are transmitted when patches are selected -- unverified) -> report it so the editor re-reads with requestPatch(); an unsolicited 01 (panel Data Dump 'one'/'bank') -> treat as an incoming patch; any 04/06/0A/0B/0C/0D/0E arriving means MIDI Echo is on -> drop it and warn. (12) sameProgram(a, b): compare bytes 8-133 only (0-7 come back as 'BNKb: nn'), treating two matrix slots as equal when both have src == 0 || dst == 0. (13) forgetBank(): nothing cached unless requestBank is implemented.
uncertain: Edit-buffer request reply: 04-4 answers with opcode 01 per KnobKraft's C++ comment ('the Matrix1000 sends edit buffers as program dumps'), but KnobKraft's Python adaptation expects 0D and Edisyn accepts both -- accept either. What byte 4 (patch number) holds in that reply is undocumented. That the reply reflects 06/0B remote edits (not just the stored patch) is assumed, not verified.

Store: Edisyn (librarian-tested) uses 0A bank + 01 num; the manual's 0E 'store edit buffer' (<num> <bank> <id>) is used by KnobKraft's C++ and was dropped by Edisyn early on without a stated reason. 0A+01 chosen as primary; both unverified here.

Reading a slot: KnobKraft sends 0A, 0C, 04-1 without a Program Change (relies on 0A setting the 'current bank' that 04-1 reads and on 0C keeping it); Edisyn instead does 0A, PC, 0C, then 04-1 (changes the sound). The no-PC path is chosen; if it returns the wrong bank on hardware, add the PC.

Checksum: Edisyn's recognizer comment says 'the Matrix 1000 doesn't transmit the checksum' (accepts 274 or 275 bytes), yet all 200 factory dumps and KnobKraft's hardware capture of patch 216 carry a correct one.
Matrix destination width: manual says 5 bits, but dest 32 (portamento time) needs 6 and a factory patch uses it; stored as a full byte 0-32.
DCO wave shape: manual says '0 = sawtooth, 31 = triangle' (6 bits); the Opcode tech pub says 0-63 with 63 = triangle and the factory data spans 0-63. 0-63 used.
LFO retrigger point: manual says 5 bits; Opcode says 0 (start) ... 63 (halfway), Edisyn and the factory data use 0-63. 0-63 used.
Mix direction: Matrix-6R manual / Opcode: 0 = DCO 2 only, 63 = DCO 1 only (Edisyn labels it 'DCO 2 <> 1'); untergeek's chart says 0 = DCO 1. Manual used.

Env 3 attack parameter number: the Matrix-1000 manual table and Edisyn/KnobKraft say 71; wolzow's transcription (and, per KnobKraft, the Matrix-6 doc) says 69. 71 used (69 would collide with Env 2 LFO trigger).
DCO 2 wave select: bits pulse/wave/noise give 0-7, but factory data only uses 0-4 (4 = noise alone); what 5-7 do is unknown. Exposed 0-4, other values preserved.
Env LFO trigger mode value 1 (gated without LFO trigger): Edisyn treats it as 'normal' and hides it; 3 factory patches use it. Exposed as its own option.

Firmware bugs: wolzow (disassembly) documents param 53 -> Env 2 amplitude and param 29 ineffective on the factory ROM; untergeek says fixed from Nordcore's 1.13 on. A gearspace quote that Bob Grieb 'confirmed the bug in 1.11, 1.13, 1.16 and 1.20' refers to Edisyn's edit-buffer report, later traced to Edisyn's own missing sign extension. Not tested on hardware.
Firmware version string for third-party ROMs in the device-ID reply (' 116', ' 120', ' 121') and whether 1.03 answers the inquiry at all: unverified.
Program Change transmission when a patch is picked on the front panel: the manual says patch changes are 'transmitted and received' on the basic channel but not when; unverified.
Pacing values (75 ms per remote edit, 100-300 ms after whole patches, 25 ms for 1.20 fast params) come from Edisyn's timings, the manual's 10 ms minimum and Tauntek's description, not measurements.
NRPN (unused here): manual says every data value is offset by 40h; KnobKraft and untergeek send VCF frequency (7-bit) raw. Only works on 1.16 / 1.20+.
Bank request filler: the manual says 50 dummy split messages follow the 100 patches; KnobKraft (confirmed with Bob Grieb's disassembly) counts 0x50 = 80.
Opcode 07 'set group mode' is documented but not implemented in the 1000's ROM (wolzow); undocumented 08/09 do it. Not used.

Keyboard mode 3 (reassign w/ rob) behaves like reassign on every firmware except Tauntek 1.21 (or the one-byte EPROM fix at 536Bh/5369h); legato portamento and single-trigger envelopes only act in unison (Opcode).
Master byte 14 (MIDI patch changes enable) has no front-panel switch in the manual; recovering it needs a reset or a master-data write.
